title: The new carrier's dead letter
prompt: A new carrier has started sending events, and the load must not stop on bad ones. The operations team wants the dead-letter output: every event the load sets aside, as it arrived, with the reason. Write `solve(shipment_events)`.
rules: Return every column of `shipment_events`, unchanged and in the same order, then `error STRING`. Events that pass every check have no row.

`error` is the first reason that applies: `missing event id` when there's no id; `bad event id` when the id without its first character can't be read as a whole number; `unknown event type` when `event_type` is missing or isn't one of `TYPES`, written exactly.
Every set-aside delivery gets its own row, repeats included.
hints: Run the starter on the sample, then find the six rows that should be set aside and why.
`F.substring("event_id", 2, 20).try_cast("int")` is NULL where the plain `cast` would fail. A chain of `F.when(...).when(...)` keeps the first reason that matches.
`isin` on a missing value gives NULL, not `False`, so a NULL `event_type` slips past `~F.col("event_type").isin(TYPES)`. Test `isNull()` too.
explanation: Each check is one condition, and a chain of `F.when` keeps the first that's true, which gives the order the team asked for. `try_cast` turns an unreadable id into NULL instead of failing the run, so `event_no.isNull()` marks a bad id once a missing id has been handled first; otherwise a missing id would come out as a bad one. The trap is the event type: `isin` on a NULL is NULL, and `~NULL` is still NULL, so an event with no type passes the check unless you also test `isNull()`. Keep repeats: the dead letter is a record of what arrived, so a bad event sent twice is there twice. Rows with no reason are filtered out last.
